findings.statement: An established Hersey/Stribeck response is the useful original reference; physiological additions do not establish a new rule.
findings.applicability: Whole participants with shared fluid panel; trial-median coefficient of friction at trial-average speed/load, not prospective control.
findings.limitations: Source full-data exponent 0.55 and fitted rheology are shared prior information, not independent verification of the same mechanism.
falsification: Separate person-only from person-and-fluid excluded validation.
Disclose author-H/rheology calibration and compare fixed-source versus train-only exponents.
Check pressure conclusions against force appearing insideH and distinguish pad photograph from loaded contact area.
findings.prior_art: The source already presents Stribeck collapse; refitting exponents repairs information fairness. No new universal friction law is supported. This review uses retained prior-art records only; it performs no new literature priority adjudication.

equation_or_program.interpretation: Executable numerical representation only; mechanism/novelty admission is assessed separately. Displayed coefficients can be rounded; exact executable states are authoritative.

variables_and_units.viscosity: Pa s at 500 s^-1; author rheology fit

findings.statement: A train-only free-exponent pressure model improves same-fluid person transfer but fails the stronger unseen-fluid transfer challenge.
findings.applicability: Whole participants with shared fluid panel; trial-median coefficient of friction at trial-average speed/load, not prospective control.
findings.limitations: Negative pressure exponent appears 9/9 folds but Hersey itself contains inverse force. Photographic area is not instantaneous loaded area; fixed fluid order and shared calibration undermine causal pressure interpretation.
falsification: Separate person-only from person-and-fluid excluded validation.
